findings.title: Time-of-Check Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) DNS Rebinding Vulnerability
findings.description: The `is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip` function in src/helpers.ts uses multiple resolution attempts with delays but still performs DNS resolution separate from the actual connection. Attackers can switch DNS responses between validation and the subsequent request, bypassing the SSRF protection.
steps_to_exploit: Set up a malicious DNS server that returns a public IP for the first query
Trigger the SSRF check in the application
Switch the DNS response to an internal IP (e.g., 127.0.0.1) for the target request
The application trusts the initial validation and makes the request to the internal service
findings.impact: Full SSRF bypass allowing unauthorized access to internal services or infrastructure.

findings.title: Incomplete Blacklist for Internal IP Ranges
findings.description: The `BAD_RANGE_USED_IN_SSRF` list in src/helpers.ts is insufficient. It misses various IPv6 local/link-local ranges (e.g., fe80::/10, fc00::/7) which can be used to scan or attack internal network infrastructure.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL targeting an IPv6 internal service (e.g., http://[fe80::1]:8080)
Submit the URL to the validation function
The validator fails to recognize the IPv6 range as internal
Application makes request to local sensitive resource
findings.impact: Bypass of SSRF protection using IPv6 address space to reach internal resources.

findings.title: Unsafe Dependency Resolution via require() in ESM Context
findings.description: The project uses CommonJS `require` for `got` in an ESM module, which is fragile and prone to dependency confusion or monkey-patching in runtime environments.
steps_to_exploit: Deploy the application in an environment where malicious packages can be hoisted
Overload the 'got' dependency with a compromised version
The 'is_redirect_safe' function will execute the malicious code during SSRF redirection checks
findings.impact: Remote code execution or sensitive information theft during validation.

findings.title: Exposure of Debug Logic in Production
findings.description: The function `is_url_safe_debug` contains sensitive logic and logs input data to the console, which could lead to information disclosure if enabled or exposed.
steps_to_exploit: Find an integration path that calls the debug function
Observe application logs to capture user-submitted URLs
Use captured data for further reconnaissance or attack planning
findings.impact: Information disclosure of internal application states and user input logs.

findings.title: Insufficient Input Normalization for Protocols
findings.description: The `is_proto_safe` function uses regex to check for the protocol, but fails to account for URI encoding or whitespace padding that might allow bypasses in downstream URL parsers.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a payload like ' javascript:alert(1)'
The trim/match sequence might fail to detect dangerous protocols depending on the library consuming the output
Browser or server misinterprets the dangerous protocol
findings.impact: Potential for XSS or protocol smuggling depending on how the validated string is consumed.

findings.title: Use of 'new URL()' on Unvalidated Input
findings.description: The `is_url_safe` function calls `new URL(u)` before full verification, which may trigger unintended side effects or resource exhaustion if the input is malformed or extremely large.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a massive string or specially crafted malformed URL to `is_url_safe`
The parser throws an exception or enters high-CPU state
Application availability is impacted via resource exhaustion
findings.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) through regex or URL parsing complexity.

findings.title: Dangerous Redirect Handling
findings.description: The `is_redirect_safe` function follows redirects using the `got` library but performs manual chain validation which can be bypassed by complex header injection or multi-step redirects.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a chain of 5+ redirects
Ensure one of the intermediate steps redirects to a local IP
The current validation logic is stateful and may lose track or improperly validate the target host of the final redirect
findings.impact: Bypass of SSRF protection during redirect following.

findings.title: Insecure Use of Shell/Exec Pattern in Workflow
findings.description: .github/workflows/njsscan.yml executes commands using `|| true` to suppress exit codes, potentially hiding vulnerabilities during CI scanning.
steps_to_exploit: Introduce malicious code into the repository
The scan runs, identifies the issue, but suppresses the error exit code
The pipeline succeeds, and vulnerable code is merged into main
findings.impact: Integration of vulnerable code due to failed security testing.

findings.title: Weak Binary IP Conversion Logic
findings.description: The `bin_ip_to_normal_ip` function allows loose binary string parsing, which could be exploited to obfuscate IPs during input validation.
steps_to_exploit: Use binary representation of local IP (e.g., 01111111000000000000000000000001)
The validator processes this as a standard IP, potentially bypassing regex checks
The downstream service resolves the obfuscated format

findings.title: Implicitly Trusted DNS Resolution
findings.description: The system resolves hostnames via local `dns` module, which is vulnerable to DNS poisoning if the environment's resolver is compromised.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a local network attack (e.g., ARP spoofing)
Intercept DNS requests to map a domain to an internal IP
The `is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip` function will report it as internal
findings.impact: The validator becomes a conduit for network reconnaissance.

findings.title: Lack of Strict Input Validation on Port Numbers
findings.description: The library focuses on host validation but ignores port number validation, allowing attackers to access internal admin panels running on high-numbered ports that might bypass basic filtering.
steps_to_exploit: Target an internal service on a non-standard port (e.g., 9000)
The URL validator focuses on the domain/IP and overlooks the port component
The application allows the request to proceed to the internal port
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to internal administrative interfaces.

findings.title: Excessive GitHub Actions Permissions
findings.description: .github/workflows/labeler.yml uses a repository-scoped token (`secrets.LABELER_TOKEN`) which has excessive permissions compared to the limited task of labeling PRs.
steps_to_exploit: Compromise a contributor account
Create a malicious PR
Use the excessive permissions of the labeler token to steal repository data or secrets

findings.title: Inconsistent Normalization of Backslashes
findings.description: The `replace_backslash_with_slash_in_string` function might not match the URL parser's normalization behavior, creating a mismatch where a backslash bypasses security checks but is interpreted as a slash by the request executor.
steps_to_exploit: Send a URL with mixed backslashes (e.g., http://localhost\@attacker.com)
The validator cleans the string but the downstream browser/server uses the original encoding
Security check bypassed

findings.title: NFKC Normalization May Create Ambiguities
findings.description: Using NFKC normalization for URLs can collapse characters in ways that are not consistent with the host's actual domain resolution, leading to 'homograph' type vulnerabilities.
steps_to_exploit: Register a domain that looks similar to an internal service under NFKC normalization
Pass this domain to the validator
The validator evaluates the normalized domain while the browser/client requests the literal domain
findings.impact: Confusion and bypass of domain-based filtering.

findings.title: Use of deprecated and potentially insecure dependencies
findings.description: The package uses `got` version 15.0.3, which has a significant history of security issues, and `ipaddr.js` 2.4.0, which may have unpatched parsing inconsistencies.
steps_to_exploit: Identify a known CVE for the specific versions of the dependencies
Target the application's reliance on these libraries during URL parsing or request execution
findings.impact: Exposure to known vulnerabilities in third-party code.
